title: Genotype-phenotype map for the flying-fish blueprint, from proxy fish, at every layer
constraint: Almost no molecular data exists for flying fish (Exocoetidae). NCBI holds one scaffold-level assembly (GCA_018398805.1, Hirundichthys speculiger) and OrthoDB holds no genome for the whole suborder Belonoidei. Every gene link here was measured in a PROXY species, zebrafish (Danio rerio) or medaka (Oryzias latipes, same order Beloniformes as flying fish). None of it is flying-fish data.
causation_warning: Most links are 'expressed in': the gene's RNA or protein was detected in the structure. That is not causation. 'required for' means a single-gene loss-of-function zebrafish has an abnormal phenotype there (or, for GO-based links, that GO places the gene in the structure's developmental process on mutant evidence). 'sufficient for' here means a verified gain-of-function allele changes the structure (e.g. enlarges it); it does not mean the gene makes the structure. No gene 'makes' a fin.

propagation_rules.expressed in: propagates UP part_of: expression in a part implies some expression in what contains it. Marked derived with the path.
propagation_rules.required for: never propagates DOWN. Propagation UP is an inference, marked derived, never presented as observed.
propagation_rules.graph: the blueprint's own part_of placements (organism-design/examples/a-flying-fish.json), which the lean thread kernel-certified as acyclic and rooted, so propagation is well defined and terminates. Bgee's own propagation is excluded: only Bgee calls that include data observed in that very structure are used.

blueprint.pectoral_fin_note: In the blueprint the pectoral fin has one tissue beneath it (mesenchyme pectoral fin) and no cell types. ZFA has 52 terms that are parts of the zebrafish pectoral fin; the blueprint has a node for none of them except the mesenchyme, so ZFIN records on those parts do not attach.

gene_breadth.note: how many blueprint nodes each gene touches by direct record; a gene in many nodes is pleiotropic, not a fin gene

gene_id_rules.note: Bgee 15.2 and ZFIN's ensembl_1_to_1 table use different Ensembl releases. A Bgee gene whose Ensembl id is absent from ZFIN's table is merged onto the ZFIN gene with exactly the same symbol; otherwise it keeps its Ensembl id as its key. Medaka genes keep Ensembl ids (no ZFIN).

convergent_substitution_in_the_papers_ow.reading: The paper's convergence table lists lat4a under medaka Ensembl id ENSORLG00000009715 with a convergent amino-acid substitution F326L present in the gliding halfbeaks E. viridis and O. micropterus and in at least 7 of 9 sequenced flying-fish species, and flags it in the fin screens. Ensembl names ENSORLG00000009715 SLC43A2 (solute carrier family 43 member 2). pathways.not_causation: Pathway membership is NOT causation and not a claim about the fin. A gene appears here because a database places it in a process or map, often computationally: GO IEA and Reactome IEA rows are electronic annotations, and every Reactome zebrafish entry is inferred by orthology from human. Membership does not show that the gene acts in that pathway in the pectoral fin, at any stage, or in a flying fish. Graded causal evidence is in genotype/causal-chains.json.

reactome.note: Reactome documentation, 'Inferred events': "we use curated human reactions to electronically infer reactions in fourteen evolutionarily divergent eukaryotic species"; homology comes from PANTHER. Every Danio rerio row in Ensembl2Reactome.txt carries evidence code IEA, and the ContentService reports isInferred: true for a Danio rerio pathway (checked on R-DRE-8866652).

causal_chains.note: Every link was produced by a subagent working under genotype/AGENT_BRIEF.md: nothing from memory, every statement from a document fetched in that run through the logged fetcher, a verbatim quote per source, and an evidence grade of association (expression only), necessity (loss of function), sufficiency (gain of function), mechanism (a pathway step shown experimentally) or hypothesis (proposed, not shown). A grade is about the link it sits on, not the gene. All of it is zebrafish or other proxy-species work: no flying-fish experiment exists. This file was merged and checked by genotype/assemble_chains.py, which upgrades nothing; validation flags travel with the data.

grades.missing: no fetched source for this link
grades.hypothesis: proposed or modelled in a paper, not shown there
grades.necessity: loss of function changes the structure or process

coverage.metric_note: chain_strength is the WEAKEST grade on a chain and is the honest measure of it: a chain is only as strong as its weakest link. genes_with_a_link_graded_X counts genes with at least one such link anywhere on the chain, which is a much weaker statement.

genes.weakest_link: process->cell_or_tissue_effect in the PECTORAL fin: the apc allele itself was assayed in the median fin fold, and the pectoral fin fold result used the GSK-3beta inhibitor BIO. The apc-specific pectoral chain therefore relies on a pharmacological stand-in plus the ring1b cross-rescue abstract.
gaps: No apc mutant data on fin rays (lepidotrichia) at all - the mutants do not survive to ray-forming stages in any fetched source.
van der Velden 2012 (PMID 22619390) is not in PMC; only the abstract was read, so the apc-ring1b-Fgf rescue cannot be quoted at figure level.

The ZFIN pectoral fin rows for apc come from a Cell paper on intestine (PMID 20850014) and a Nature paper on cardiac valves (PMID 14534590) whose abstracts do not mention fins; only the curated rows support them.

Bhattacharya 2018 full text could not be retrieved (Europe PMC fullTextXML HTTP 500 for PMC6288381; NCBI PMC efetch publisher-blocked), so which Wnt inhibitor was used for the segment-length experiment is unknown from fetched text.
No fetched source reports LiCl or IWR-1 by name in an apc fin experiment.

chain.from: apc (ZDB-GENE-031112-7)
chain.to: Apc as a component of the beta-catenin destruction complex; loss of Apc raises nuclear beta-catenin in the fin epithelium
chain.experiment_type: germline mutant (apcCA50a) with anti-beta-catenin immunostaining and nuclear-intensity quantification; parallel GSK-3beta inhibitor (BIO) pharmacology; IWR (inhibitor of Wnt response) and heat-shock dkk1 for the loss-of-signalling arm
chain.stage: 30 hpf and 36 hpf (embryo; ZFIN Pharyngula:Prim-25 for the curated rows)

sources.quote: For gain-of-function studies, we used apc mutant (Paridaen et al., 2009) and a chemical inhibitor of GSK-3β called BIO (Gore et al., 2011); both APC and GSK3β are components of the β-catenin destruction complex
We observed an appreciable increase in nuclear β-catenin in the fin epithelium of apc mutants, as well as in BIO-treated embryos at 36 hpf and 30 hpf, respectively (Fig. 2E-H′).
Truncation of the tumour suppressor adenomatous polyposis coli (Apc) constitutively activates the Wnt/beta-catenin signalling pathway.

chain.from: constitutive nuclear beta-catenin
chain.to: graded canonical Wnt transcriptional output along the proximo-distal axis that sets laminin alpha5 levels, and, in the fin bud, sustains Fgf signalling
chain.experiment_type: qRT-PCR and in situ for laminin genes in apc mutant / BIO / HS:dkk1-GFP; lama5 and itga3 morpholino epistasis; genetic rescue of the ring1b fin phenotype by the apc mutation
chain.stage: 16-36 hpf (laminin arm); fin bud outgrowth stages (ring1b epistasis)

sources.quote: Interestingly, apc mutant and BIO-treated embryos exhibited an increase and an expansion of lama5 expression in the fin fold (Fig. 7D-G′).

Indeed, upon knockdown of lamα5 in both apc mutant and BIO-treated embryos, the cells show relatively lower aspect ratios and were far less stretched when compared with the control embryos (Fig. 7J-M).
Exogenous application of FGF4, as well as enhanced stimulation of Fgf signaling by overactivated Wnt signaling in apc mutants, partially restores the fin developmental program.

chain.from: excess canonical Wnt output and raised laminin alpha5
chain.to: loss of the proximo-distal epithelial cell-shape pattern of the fin fold: all basal epithelial cells become stretched, sub-epidermal space fails to form, fin fold is reduced
chain.experiment_type: E-cadherin immunostaining with cell aspect-ratio quantification in apc mutants and in BIO-treated embryos; local BIO bead application; hydroxyurea/aphidicolin proliferation control
chain.stage: 30 hpf and 36 hpf (median fin fold); 5 dpf (pectoral fin)

sources.quote: Further cell shape analysis revealed that the epithelial cells throughout the PD axis of the fin fold exhibit stretched morphology by 36 hpf in apc mutants and by 30 hpf in BIO-treated embryos (Fig. 2I-N).
Furthermore, the gain of Wnt signalling by BIO treatment resulted in reduction of the pectoral fin fold and all the cells along the PD axis showed a stretched morphology (Fig. 8D-F).

Our results show that the epithelia of both median and pectoral fin are patterned by canonical Wnt signalling along the PD axis, further suggesting that this developmental mechanism is conserved in both unpaired and paired fin appendages.

genes.weakest_link: process->cell_or_tissue_effect: the collagen fibril disorganisation was measured by TEM in skin, bone and intervertebral space, not in the pectoral fin, so the mechanistic bridge from reduced GAG to the malformed fin radial is inferred across tissues within the same mutant.
gaps: No signalling-pathway assay in b3galt6 mutants, so the thread cannot say which pathway a GAG-linkage defect perturbs in the fin.
No chondrocyte-level or osteoblast-level readout in the pectoral fin (no cell counts, proliferation or differentiation markers), so no evidence reaches a cell node.
GAG measurements are from adult bone, muscle and skin; no GAG quantification from fin tissue at the larval stages when the radials are patterned.
Only one allele (cmg20) is reported in ZFIN for the fin phenotypes; no second independent allele and no rescue.

sources.quote: Here, we show that CRISPR/Cas9-mediated b3galt6 knock-out zebrafish, lacking galactosyltransferase II, which adds the third sugar in the linkage region, largely recapitulate the phenotypic abnormalities seen in human beta3GalT6-deficiency disorders.

Coupling is the relevant variable: "ionic coupling assays revealed allele-specific differences in coupling efficiency and gating ... measurable differences in Cx43 function may be correlated with the severity of defects in bone length" (Hoptak-Solga et al. 2007, FEBS Lett, PMID 17599838, doi 10.1016/j.febslet.2007.06.030).

connexin_and_fin_length.relation_to_potassium_channel_story: The fetched sources DO connect the two stories experimentally in one place: Seaver et al. 2025 (PMID 40912447, doi 10.1016/j.ydbio.2025.09.001) report that 'the increased segment length in response to Xl-Kcna5 overexpression requires Cx43' and conclude 'potassium channels act together with gap junction channels to influence joint formation, and therefore skeletal patterning, in the zebrafish regenerating fin'. A second, preprint-only source (Aramaki & Kondo 2024, doi 10.1101/2024.03.27.587111) puts a hyperactive kcnk5b and a dominant-negative Cx43 under the same cell-type-specific promoters and finds the keratinocyte manipulations change fin size while the osteoblast manipulations change fin ray segment length. Jiang et al. 2024 (PMID 38527087) place Kcnk5b upstream of shha in the pectoral fin bud and PROPOSE, without testing, that gap junctions explain the uniform intracellular K+ within the bud. What the sources DO NOT connect: (1) the channel in the Seaver epistasis is a Xenopus kcna5 transgene, not zebrafish kcnk5b, kcnh2a or kcnj13, so no fetched paper shows a zebrafish fin-length K+ channel allele interacting genetically with gja1b; (2) nothing links gja5a - the connexin with the flying-fish convergent substitution - to fin length, fin ray length or segment length in any species; (3) no fetched source puts a connexin and a potassium channel in the same cell of the pectoral fin by co-expression or co-localisation. On the flying-fish side, the Daane 2021 claim was verified independently from the fetched Data S1 (mmc2.xlsx): sheet 'G - conv. aa subst.' lists gja5a (ENSORLG00000017925) with substitution G329V ticked for E. viridis, O. micropterus and Exocoetidae and ticked in 'fin screens' - so the thread's gja5a claim is CONFIRMED. But the main text's only connexin statement is about a different gene and the opposite signature: 'the gap junction protein cx43, mutations in which cause short fins in zebrafish, is under constrained sequence evolution along the ancestral branch of flying fishes' (sheet 'J - Exocoeidae phylop' lists cx43 as 'con', phyloP p = 0). gja5a is therefore convergently substituted while cx43 is constrained; they are different genes and the paper makes no functional claim about either in fin length. ZFIN's wild-type expression file has no fin or fin-cell record for gja5a at all (brain, heart, vasculature, somite, skeletal muscle, pharyngeal arches), whereas gja1b is recorded in pectoral fin, pectoral fin cartilage, fin fold pectoral fin bud, mesenchyme and regenerating fin.

sources.quote: Here, we provide insights into how Cx43, expressed medially, influences changes in gene expression in lateral skeletal precursor cells. In this report, we demonstrate that the sof phenotype is caused by mutations in the connexin43 (cx43) gene.

Finally, targeted gene knockdown of cx43 in adult regenerating fins recapitulates the sof(b123) phenotype, revealing that the loss of Cx43 is sufficient to reduce both cell proliferation and segment length. We hypothesize that the level of gap junctional intercellular communication among dividing cells regulates the level of cell proliferation and ultimately regulates bone growth.

Mutations in the zebrafish connexin43 (cx43) gene cause the short fin phenotype, indicating that direct cell-cell communication contributes to bone length. ... refuted_or_unsupported.proposed: The tetrapod AER/mesenchyme feedback loop runs on Fgf AND Wnt signals in both directions in the zebrafish pectoral fin.
refuted_or_unsupported.finding: The Fgf arms are supported in zebrafish, but the Wnt arm is explicitly NOT established there. Leerberg 2019 states that the Wnt-mediated induction of AER Fgfs known from chick and mouse 'has yet to be established in zebrafish'. No paper I fetched shows a Wnt ligand from one of these two tissues acting on a receptor in the other in the zebrafish pectoral fin. (The ZFIN wildtype-expression table in C:/Temp/genotype/raw/ does place wnt7aa in ZFA:0000085, the pectoral fin bud AER, from ZDB-PUB-120529-34 = PMID 22619390, but that paper is not open access and its abstract does not mention wnt7aa, so I could not quote the expression claim from a fetched document, and no receptor or function is attached to it.)

refuted_or_unsupported.proposed: The ZPA is the source of anteroposterior positional information in the zebrafish pectoral fin bud, as Shh is in the tetrapod limb.

In shh-null sonic you mutants some aspects of anteroposterior polarity are set up WITHOUT Shh and only later depend on it for maintenance, so the zebrafish ZPA is not the sole source of anteroposterior information. Separately, the Shh/ZPA module does not account for ray branching: Braunstein 2021 found Shh/Smo inhibition from 2 dpf left the normal complement of 18 caudal rays, and the caudal fin has no polarised shha at all.

sources.title: Transient establishment of anteroposterior polarity in the zebrafish pectoral fin bud in the absence of sonic hedgehog activity.
sources.quote: We show that Shh is required for the establishment of some aspects of anteroposterior polarity, while other aspects of anteroposterior polarity are established independently of Shh, and only later come to depend on Shh for their maintenance.

sources.title: Basal epidermis collective migration and local Sonic hedgehog signaling promote skeletal branching morphogenesis in zebrafish fins
sources.quote: Zebrafish shha expression studies suggest a ZPA patterns pectoral and other paired fins but not unpaired fins including the caudal fin (; ).

sources.title: Basal epidermis collective migration and local Sonic hedgehog signaling promote skeletal branching morphogenesis in zebrafish fins
sources.quote: As such, Shh/Smo may have limited or no role in pre-patteming the caudal fin field despite early shha and ptch2 expression.

refuted_or_unsupported.proposed: Shh from the fin basal epidermis drives proliferation of the underlying skeletal progenitors during ray growth and regeneration.
refuted_or_unsupported.finding: Refuted for proliferation. Braunstein 2021 found no change in EdU+ intra-ray cells under Smoothened inhibition and states that earlier pro-proliferative conclusions may have been cyclopamine off-target effects; the Shh/Smo requirement is dedicated to ray branching, by mechanically coupling epidermal cells to pre-osteoblasts, with outgrowth, joints and osteoblast differentiation intact.

sources.title: Basal epidermis collective migration and local Sonic hedgehog signaling promote skeletal branching morphogenesis in zebrafish fins
sources.quote: BMS-treatment of 29 dpf shha:GFP fish exposed to EdU for 12 hours did not change the fraction of EdU+ intra-ray cells, i.e. pObs and mesenchyme nestled between the epidermal Shh+ domains of each hemi-ray

sources.title: Basal epidermis collective migration and local Sonic hedgehog signaling promote skeletal branching morphogenesis in zebrafish fins
sources.quote: Notably, previous conclusions that Shh/Smo signaling is a pro-proliferative factor in regenerating fins (; ) may reflect off-target cyclopamine effects ().

refuted_or_unsupported.proposed: wnt10a signalling maintains the pectoral fin fold (ZFA:0005317).
refuted_or_unsupported.finding: Shown for the MEDIAN fin fold, not the pectoral fin fold. wnt10a mutants collapse the median fin fold and fail adult unpaired fin metamorphosis; the abstract reports no pectoral fin fold phenotype, and the mechanism is loss of distal character (dlx2a, then col1a1a and other ECM genes) and actinotrichia positioning, not a named ligand acting on a receptor in a second tissue.

sources.title: wnt10a is required for zebrafish median fin fold maintenance and adult unpaired fin metamorphosis.
sources.quote: wnt10a mutant zebrafish embryos display impaired tooth development and a collapsing median fin fold (MFF). Rescue experiments show that wnt10a is essential for MFF maintenance both during embryogenesis and later metamorphosis.

refuted_or_unsupported.proposed: HGF/MET is the conserved signal that pulls muscle precursors into the paired fin, so it can be assumed for any fish fin.
refuted_or_unsupported.finding: It holds in zebrafish (met CRISPR null loses pectoral abductor muscle) but not across gnathostomes: in shark, Hgf and Met are not expressed at the right time or place for fin muscle precursor delamination and migration.

sources.title: Stepwise participation of HGF/MET signaling in the development of migratory muscle precursors during vertebrate evolution
sources.quote: However, these genes were not expressed at the right time in the right place to allow them to be involved in the delamination and migration of paired fin myoblasts in shark embryos. Shark Hgf mRNA was detectable only in the posterior part of pectoral fin buds after the entrance of pectoral fin muscle precursors in the fin buds.

gaps.gap: No fetched zebrafish single-cell study of fin tissue reports a cell-cell communication / ligand-receptor analysis for these cell types. Cudak et al. 2024 (PMID 38318374, iScience) scRNA-seq's FACS-enriched epidermal, osteoblast and blastemal fin regenerate cells, and Robbins et al. 2023 scRNA-seq's the regenerating fin, but neither full text contains CellChat, CellPhoneDB, NicheNet, Omnipath, 'ligand-receptor' or 'cell-cell communication'; the same is true of the 2026 Nature Communications fin/limb regeneration multi-omic paper (PMC12923738). Targeted EPMC searches for zebrafish fin scRNA-seq plus CellChat/CellPhoneDB/ligand-receptor returned no such study.

No ligand-receptor database was fetched, so no database-derived pair is recorded. CellChatDB is human and mouse: 'Applying CellChat to mouse and human skin datasets shows its ability to extract complex signaling patterns' (Jin et al. 2021, Nat Commun, PMID 33597522, doi 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9). Any pair taken from it for a fin cell type would be orthology-inferred and none was needed, because every pair recorded here has a zebrafish-native source except the CXCL12/CXCR4 record.

The Cell Ontology, as served by Ubergraph, places NO marker gene in any of the six cell types. A SPARQL query over CL:0000062 (osteoblast), CL:0000138 (chondrocyte), CL:0000058 (chondroblast), CL:0000134 (mesenchymal cell), CL:0000362 (epidermal cell) and CL:0000056 (myoblast) for any outgoing property whose label contains 'marker' or 'express' returned HTTP 200 with zero bindings.

Bgee has no cell-type-resolved call for any of these genes. In Danio_rerio_expr_advanced.tsv.gz, shha, smo and ptch2 are 'present, gold quality' in pectoral fin (UBERON:0000151), paired fin bud (UBERON:0002531), mesenchyme pectoral fin (UBERON:0003934) and pectoral fin lepidotrichium (UBERON:4000175), but every call is an UBERON anatomical entity, never a CL cell type. gja1b, gja5a, gja5b, panx1a and gjd4 have NO Bgee call for any fin or cleithrum anatomical entity. The Bgee SPARQL endpoint remains refused (HTTP 403) per the brief, so no cell-type query could be run there.

Nothing establishes an interaction involving chondrocyte (ZFA:0001161+ZFA:0009084, ZFA:0000141+ZFA:0009084) or chondroblast (ZFA:0000257+ZFA:0009027) as sender or receiver. ZFIN records gja1b wild-type expression in pectoral fin cartilage (ZFA:0000257) by in situ at Larval:Protruding-mouth, but that is expression, not an interaction, and the source abstract (Chatterjee et al. 2005, PMID 15895415) does not mention fin or cartilage. No gap-junction, contact or ligand-receptor partner for fin cartilage cells was found.

Nothing establishes any interaction for the cleithrum, including cleithrum / osteoblast (ZFA:0000184+ZFA:0009031). No fetched source mentions a connexin, gap junction or ligand-receptor pair in the cleithrum or pectoral girdle.

No fetched source establishes an interaction for pectoral fin fold / mesenchymal cell (ZFA:0005317+ZFA:0009081) or pectoral fin fold / epidermal cell (ZFA:0005317+ZFA:0009183) specifically; the epidermis-osteoblast records are for the fin ray / basal epidermis, not the fin fold.

Pannexins are untested in the fin. ZFIN lists panx1a^nhi6, panx1b^nhi7, panx2^sa12329 and panx3^sa10093/sa12358 alleles, but phenoGeneCleanData_fish.txt records no fin, fin ray or segment phenotype for any panx gene, and no fetched paper reports one.

Connexins other than gja1b have no fin-length phenotype in the fetched record. ZFIN fin/fin-ray phenotypes exist only for gja1b; gja4 alleles give pigment-stripe phenotypes, gja3 cardiac and eye, and gja5a/gja5b none in the fin. gjd4/Cx46.8 couples trunk slow muscle (PMID 38936363) but was not examined in the fin.

No fetched source shows gap-junction coupling between an osteoblast and an epidermal cell, or between a myoblast and any other fin cell type, in the fin. The Aramaki & Kondo preprint manipulates each cell type separately and does not demonstrate transfer between them.

The dmh35 fin-ray and segment phenotype could only be taken from ZFIN's curated annotation, not from the paper's own words: the publisher blocks PMC full text for Henke et al. 2017/2018 (Genetics, PMID 28835471, PMC5629327; efetch returns 'The publisher of this article does not allow downloading of the full text in XML form') and the abstract does not name gja1b. ZFIN rows (phenoGeneCleanData_fish.txt, ZDB-FISH-180503-22, ZDB-PUB-170825-12): 'gja1b | ZFA:0001554 lepidotrichium | PATO:0002364 shortened', 'gja1b | ZFA:0005633 lepidotrichium segment | PATO:0002364 shortened', 'gja1b | ZFA:0005596 paired fin | PATO:0002364 shortened', 'gja1b | ZFA:0005597 median fin | PATO:0002364 shortened'.

No fetched source measures the PECTORAL fin specifically for the cx43 segment-length phenotype. Iovine 2005, Hoptak-Solga 2007/2008, Sims 2009 and Bhattacharya 2021 all measure caudal fin rays; the only pectoral-fin statement is the ZFIN curated 'paired fin shortened' for gja1b^dmh35/+.

No flying-fish (Exocoetidae) molecular or expression data for any connexin, pannexin or ligand-receptor pair; everything here is zebrafish proxy data, and the Daane 2021 gja5a entry is a comparative-genomic substitution call only, with no functional test in any species.

A ligand-receptor pair for a Wnt arrow in either direction between the zebrafish pectoral fin bud AER (ZFA:0000085) and its mesenchyme (ZFA:0000789 / ZFA:0001000). In tetrapod limbs ectodermal Wnt3/Wnt3a and AER Wnt/beta-catenin sit inside the Fgf8/Fgf10 loop; Leerberg 2019 says this has yet to be established in zebrafish.

A Bmp arrow between the AER and the mesenchyme of the zebrafish pectoral fin bud. bmp2b, bmp4 and bmp16 sit in the ZFIN expression list for ZFA:0000085 and bmp4 for ZFA:0001000, and Jiang 2024 shows bmp4 and its target msx2b respond to K+ in the bud, but I found no zebrafish pectoral-fin source placing a Bmp ligand in one of the two tissues and a Bmp receptor (bmpr1aa, bmpr1ba, acvr1l) in the other with a loss- or gain-of-function test.

A dorsoventral arrow from the bud ectoderm to the mesenchyme. wnt7a->Lmx1b (ectoderm to mesenchyme) and En1 in the ventral ectoderm are standard in tetrapod limbs, and wnt7aa and en1a do appear in the ZFIN AER expression list for ZFA:0000085, but I found no zebrafish pectoral-fin functional source, so no arrow.
Gremlin/Grem1-type Bmp antagonism closing the Shh-Fgf loop. I reached it only in mouse (Michos 2007, and in the kidney at that), not in the zebrafish pectoral fin.

A ray-to-interray or interray-to-ray signalling arrow in the ADULT pectoral fin. The interray tissue appears in the fetched sources only as a place where rcan2 is expressed during regeneration (Jiang 2024) and as part of a bioelectric size pathway (Lanni 2019, title only); I found no source naming a ligand in one compartment and a receptor in the other, in either direction, in any fin let alone the pectoral.

Any pectoral-fin REGENERATION source for the epidermis-to-blastema and blastema-to-epidermis arrows. Every regeneration paper I could reach (Poss 2000, Shibata 2016, Wehner 2014, Armstrong 2017, Laforest 1998) used the caudal fin; those arrows are recorded with caudal-fin or fin-generic nodes and must not be drawn inside the pectoral fin without that caveat.

An arrow to or from the pectoral fin MUSCULATURE (ZFA:0000563) after the myoblasts have arrived. The only musculature arrow I could support is the HGF/MET immigration arrow into the bud; I found no zebrafish source for a signal from differentiated pectoral fin muscle to the skeleton, the tendon attachment or the epidermis, nor for a signal to the muscle from the fin skeleton. The Lbx1/Fgf link ('FGF signalling from within the fin bud controls the Lbx1 phosphorylation state') appears only as a citation inside Nord 2019; I did not reach the primary paper.

A signalling arrow to or from the pectoral fin CARTILAGE (ZFA:0000257) at the chondrocyte level. Hedgehog reaches the endoskeletal disc and sets radial number (Tanaka 2024, Lalonde 2018), but I found no zebrafish source for an Ihh/Pthlh-type chondrocyte-to-perichondrium arrow, nor for a cartilage-to-epidermis or cartilage-to-muscle arrow in the pectoral fin.
The S1P receptor in the fin mesenchyme and the specific robo paralogue in the AER for the Slit-Robo/S1P loop (Mahabaleshwar 2022): the paper is not open access and the abstract names neither.
A ligand-receptor pair for the somite-derived apical-fold-inducing cells acting on the AER (Masselink 2016): the abstract reports cell invasion and ablation, not a paracrine signal.

An arrow involving the pectoral fin fold (ZFA:0005317) or the fin fold of the bud (ZFA:0005316) as the SENDER to the epidermis or to the AER. The fin-fold arrows I found run mesenchyme-to-AER (slit3), AER-to-mesenchyme (S1P) and fin-fold-mesenchyme-to-cartilage (ablation); the fin fold as an epithelial signalling tissue in its own right is unsupported here.
Any flying-fish source at all. Every arrow here is zebrafish (with one shark/mouse/chick comparison) and must be presented as a proxy for the enlarged pectoral fin, never as flying-fish data.

interventions.note: Every entry is a manipulation that was SHOWN in an experiment, or is explicitly graded hypothesis where a paper only proposes it. All of it is proxy-species work, overwhelmingly zebrafish: no genetic manipulation has ever been done in a flying fish, so nothing here is a flying-fish result. A flying fish's wing is an enlarged pectoral fin. `usable_as_a_calibrated_knob` is true only where a paper gives BOTH a number and the stage it was measured at; most of this literature reports morphology in figure panels, so most entries carry the paper's words instead of a value and the Studio must not interpolate one. Stages fall into non-interpolable regimes (embryonic fin bud against reproductively mature adult): an effect measured in one does not transfer to the other. Pleiotropy is computed from the vetted map, not from the papers.

levels.coding: a change in the protein-coding sequence (allele, amino-acid substitution)
levels.cis-regulatory or expression: a change in where or how much the gene is expressed, without changing the protein
levels.TF dosage: a change in the amount of a transcription factor
levels.epigenetic: a change in chromatin state or silencing
levels.pharmacological: a drug or inhibitor, with its dose where the source gives one

paralog_guards.rule: After the teleost genome duplication zebrafish often carries two paralogs, and this project found no cross-rescue for any of the pairs below. The Studio must never offer a route for one paralog on evidence gathered for the other, and must never present either as the flying-fish gene: orthology to a flying-fish gene is an assumption nowhere established here.

tbx5a.note: Teleost-specific whole-genome duplication left zebrafish with two TBX5 genes, tbx5a and tbx5b. Parrie 2013 (PMID 23441045): "Our phylogenetic analyses confirm tbx5b as a paralog that likely arose in the teleost-specific whole genome duplication ~270 MYA" and "injection of wild-type mRNA from one tbx5 paralog was not sufficient to cross-rescue phenotypes of the paralogous gene". Every tbx5a result below is tbx5a-specific and must NOT be transferred to tbx5b: the two have non-overlapping fin requirements (tbx5a = initiation, tbx5b = later outgrowth timing).

fgf10a.note: Zebrafish has two fgf10 genes from the whole-genome duplication. Yan 2015: "Due to whole genome duplication, the zebrafish has two fgf10 orthologs, fgf10a and fgf10b" and "While fgf10a has a role in development of the esophagus and swimbladder, we found in the present study that fgf10b had a complementary expression pattern in the liver, pancreas, and gut". Nothing in any fetched source places fgf10b in the pectoral fin or gives it a fin phenotype, so the fin role is fgf10a-specific and must not be generalised to fgf10b. The fin mutant allele daedalus (dae, tbvbo) is an fgf10a allele (Norton 2005).

shha.note: Fishes carry a shha paralog, shhb (tiggy winkle hedgehog), with a diverged cis-regulatory module. Hadzhiev 2007: "We demonstrate that the sonic hedgehog a ( shha ) paralogs sonic hedgehog b ( tiggy winkle hedgehog ; shhb ) genes of fishes have a modified ar-C enhancer, which specifies a diverged function at the embryonic midline" and "Altering and exchanging motifs between paralog enhancers resulted in reversal of enhancer specificity in the floor plate and notochord". No fetched source places shhb in the pectoral fin bud or gives it a fin phenotype, and the diverged enhancer is direct evidence that paralog expression domains are partitioned - so no shha fin result may be transferred to shhb. The fin mutant allele sonic you (syu, tq252) is a shha allele.

pax7a.note: teleost-duplication paralogs; evidence on one is not evidence for the other

paralog_guards.tbx5a_tbx5b_specifically: Asked for by the hub. tbx5a is the pectoral fin initiation gene whose null never develops a fin bud, and it also builds the heart (its mutant is 'heartstrings'), so it is the worst pleiotropy case in the set. tbx5b has ZERO experimental molecular-function evidence (its GO annotation is inferred by ancestry only) and no sub-organ phenotype. Neither gene has an intervention entry in this file yet, because no interventions extraction has been run for them; until one is, the Studio has no sourced tbx5 route of any kind and must offer none.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: pectoral fin length
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No fetched source measures pectoral fin length for any gja1b allele. The only pectoral-relevant record is ZFIN's curated qualitative 'paired fin (ZFA:0005596) | shortened' for gja1b^dmh35/+ (PMID 28835471, full text publisher-blocked). Every quantitative cx43 fin measurement in the fetched record is on the caudal fin: Iovine/Hoptak-Solga/Sims/Bhattacharya/Seaver all amputate and measure the caudal fin, and Sims' and Seaver's measurements are on a single named caudal ray (V+3 and third-most dorsal respectively). Do not transfer a caudal segment number to the pectoral fin in the Studio without labelling it an assumption.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: fin area or span
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No sourced genetic route through a connexin. Hoptak-Solga 2008 gives a whole-fin number ('half the length') but no area or span, and no fetched source measures fin area or span for any gja1b allele. The one source that claims a connexin/K+ manipulation moves 'fin size' is the Aramaki and Kondo preprint, abstract-only and unverifiable, and it does not define or quantify fin size.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: ray segment number
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: Not measured as a count in any fetched source. The literature treats segment length and segment addition as separate mechanisms - Seaver 2025 states 'genetic mechanisms controlling segment length are independent of genetic mechanisms controlling segment addition' (citing Iovine et al. 2000) - but no fetched source reports a segment number for a cx43 allele. The nearest thing is Sims 2009's 'frequency of joint formation', which is reported as a segment-length distribution, not a count.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: ray branching / bifurcation
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No connexin route. The fetched route to branching is the shha/Smo basal-epidermis-to-pre-osteoblast interaction (Braunstein 2021, PMID 34038742) and the Fraser complex (fras1, preprint), neither of which is a connexin or a bidirectional lever.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: fin ray length in a flying fish or any non-model species
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No molecular or functional data for any connexin in Exocoetidae. Daane 2021's cx43 entry is a sequence-conservation call ('con', phyloP p = 0) and its gja5a entry is a convergent-substitution call; neither is a functional test, and gja5a is deliberately excluded here because it is not the fin-length connexin.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: cell-type-restricted segment-length control with a verified source
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: Only the Aramaki and Kondo preprint restricts the manipulation to keratinocytes versus osteoblasts, and it is abstract-only. Every peer-reviewed intervention here is either germline (alleles) or systemic/local but not cell-type-restricted (hsp70 promoter, morpholino, GAP27 peptide).

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: fin area or span increased above wild type (the gliding-relevant direction)
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No intervention in this set increases any fin dimension beyond wild type. Every sourced effect is a decrease, or a partial rescue back toward wild type (prdm1a WT-mRNA +12% cleithrum, Prdm1a-dSET +38% scapulocoracoid area, both measured against the mutant, not against wild type). The only gain-of-function arms are the SHFM PRDM1 variants, which make the endoskeletal disk smaller, and sox9a/sox9b mRNA injection, which was scored on transcripts and not on fin morphology. For the Design Studio this means the TF-dosage and epigenetic levers in my set are enlargement-negative only: they can shrink a fin, not enlarge one.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: adult fin size, span or aspect ratio
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No sourced route. Every effect in this set is scored between 24 hpf and 13 dpf. The ezh2 maternal-zygotic mutant dies at 48 hpf and the rnf2 null at 4-5 dpf, i.e. before fin skeletal maturation, so these two levers can never report an adult fin parameter. No fish size or body length is given in any source fetched.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: pectoral fin lepidotrichium (ZFA:0001551) or actinotrichium (ZFA:0005545) number or length
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No sourced route in this set. No paper fetched reports a ray or actinotrichium measurement for any of these five genes; prdm1a's most distal measured structure is the fin fold and the endoskeletal disk.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: pectoral fin radial number or length (ZFA:0001586)
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No sourced route. Radials are not scored in any source fetched for prdm1a, sox9a, rnf2, ezh2 or hdac1.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: pectoral fin musculature (ZFA:0000563) mass or fibre type
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No sourced route. The only fin-muscle observation is incidental and qualitative: in rnf2 mutants 'a few MF20-positive cells, presumably pectoral fin muscle progenitors, were detected'. No muscle parameter was measured for any of the five genes.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: fin insertion position, fin angle or fin attachment on the body wall
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No sourced route. No source fetched reports a positional or angular fin parameter; all readouts are length, area, presence or ossification.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: fin enlargement by cis-regulatory change (enhancer edit)
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No sourced route at the level of a specific sequence. The only cis-regulatory element with a named motif in this set is the mouse Col2a1 intron-1 48-bp enhancer with three HMG-like sites bound by SOX9, which is mouse and not zebrafish, and no nucleotide sequence is given in the abstract fetched. The prdm1a CUT&RUN peaks give named Hox motifs for the whole peak set but no sequence, and no peak was functionally tested as an enhancer. Do not let the Design Studio offer an enhancer edit for these genes.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: pectoral fin length
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No source fetched in this run measures pectoral fin length (proximal-distal or longest-axis length) in any mutant of these five genes. Koudijs 2005 measured dorsoventral extent and area only, and explicitly found the anterior-posterior extent unchanged in hhip mutants. Tanaka 2024 reports an AP:PD shape change of the endoskeletal disc, not a fin length.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: fin ray (lepidotrichium, ZFA:0001551) number
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: Tanaka 2024 states 'Zebrafish with hhip mutations are known to exhibit an increase in the number of fin rays and an enlarged pectoral fin primordia' but attributes this to Koudijs 2005 and van Eeden 1996 and does not measure it; neither the Koudijs full text nor the van Eeden abstract fetched here reports a fin ray count. The ZFIN row 'pectoral fin has extra parts of type' for hhip<sup>tc256d</sup> in the adult is the closest record but carries no count. No sourced route with a number.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: actinotrichium (ZFA:0005545) number or length
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No fetched source reports actinotrichia in any mutant of these five genes.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: pectoral fin musculature (ZFA:0000563), vasculature (ZFA:0005096), nerve (ZFA:0005436)
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No fetched source reports a fin muscle, vessel or nerve phenotype for these genes. Ochi 2006 shows hhip acts on slow versus fast muscle fate but in the trunk adaxial cells, not in the fin.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: apical ectodermal ridge (ZFA:0000085) and zone of polarizing activity (ZFA:0001451) extent
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No fetched source assays either node in a mutant of hhip, ptch1, disp1, cyp26a1 or rerea. The only evidence at these nodes is from shh (Neumann 1999) and fgf16 (Nomura 2006) experiments, so no gene in this set gives a sourced lever on them.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: pectoral fin area or radial number as a function of retinoic acid dose
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No fetched source gives a retinoic acid or RA-inhibitor concentration, so the RA axis has a sourced stage window (early gastrula through the six- to eight-somite stages) but no sourced dose. DEAB is not named in any fetched source and must not be displayed.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: radial number from a pharmacological intervention
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: Cyclopamine rescue experiments in the only paper that performed them scored eye and ear, never the fin skeleton, and Tanaka 2024 performed no drug experiment. There is therefore no pharmacological route to a radial-number change, only a genetic one (hhip loss).

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: any cis-regulatory, TF-dosage or epigenetic intervention on a fin parameter
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: Every fin-parameter intervention sourced here is coding (nonsense or frameshift), morpholino knockdown, or pharmacological. No enhancer deletion, no promoter variant and no epigenetic manipulation of these five genes with a fin readout was found. Tanaka 2024 notes that 'regulatory enhancers may also regulate the strength of Hedgehog signaling' but tested none. The CRISPR knock-in EGFP alleles are reporters, not regulatory interventions.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: pectoral fin area, span or aspect ratio
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: Every adult measurement in all fetched sources for these three genes is a LENGTH (fin length, normalized to standard length) or a segment length. No paper measures pectoral fin area, span, chord or aspect ratio. The only area measurement anywhere in the set is Jiang 2024's pectoral fin BUD area at 32-56 hpf, standardized to eye or otic vesicle area, which is an embryonic bud, not the adult fin blade. A Design Studio slider for fin area or span therefore has no sourced genetic route in this gene set.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: pectoral fin ray number
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No fetched source reports a change in the NUMBER of pectoral fin rays (lepidotrichia) for kcnk5b, kcnh2a or slc43a2a. Perathoner 2014 reports segment number per ray (unchanged in alf, increased in lof and rapunzel), and ZFIN carries one contradictory 'lepidotrichium segment / increased amount' row, but ray count itself is never measured.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: pectoral fin insertion position, angle or orientation
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: Nothing in the fetched set manipulates or measures where the pectoral fin attaches or at what angle. Daane 2021 notes the flying-fish caudal fin asymmetry aids above-water propulsion, but no gene in this set is tied to fin position.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: pectoral fin musculature or muscle mass
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: No intervention in this gene set reports a muscle phenotype. Jiang 2024 notes the fin bud forms 'endochondral bone, musculature, and other tissues at the proximal base of the fin', but no muscle measurement follows from any kcnk5b, kcnh2a or slc43a2a manipulation. Guetg 2015 explicitly found no Lat4 protein in mouse skeletal muscle.

no_sourced_genetic_route.parameter: body length (standard length) under kcnk5b or kcnh2a manipulation
no_sourced_genetic_route.note: Only slc43a2a has a sourced body-length result (nr21: no statistically decreased body size). For kcnk5b, ZFIN carries a 'whole organism / shape abnormal' row and Perathoner 2014 compared 'fish of similar standard length' as a control rather than reporting SL as an outcome; Haffter 1996's abstract reports dominant body-length reductions for four unnamed mutations, not for alf. summary.honest_reading: No requirement has a route that reaches it. Three of the four are 'partial', and in each case the partial route answers a different question from the one asked: for the fin, a 1.65-fold area increase against the 3.9-fold required, with span and aspect ratio never measured at all; for the muscle, an increment on existing trunk muscle rather than an allocation to the pectoral fin, which no manipulation has ever been shown to enlarge; for air breathing, an anatomy that living fishes have evolved at least nine times over but whose construction genetics is mostly correlative and entirely absent for the flying fish's own order. Oxygen delivery is a flat 'none', and the Lean thread's kernel-checked elimination puts the shortfall at about 26-fold on a product of three physiological quantities that genetics does not report. The useful result of this exercise is the map of where the biology is missing, not a buildable design.

flier_genome.constraint: Almost no molecular data exists for flying fish (Exocoetidae). NCBI holds one scaffold-level assembly (GCA_018398805.1, Hirundichthys speculiger) and OrthoDB holds no genome for the whole suborder Belonoidei. Every gene link here was measured in a PROXY species, zebrafish (Danio rerio) or medaka (Oryzias latipes, same order Beloniformes as flying fish). None of it is flying-fish data. No bird data is used anywhere: class Aves is this project's held-out clade, so bird flight-muscle and respiratory genetics are excluded by construction.

items.requirement: pectoral lifting area about 3.9 times the real fish's and span about 2.5 times, at a similar aspect ratio
items.verdict: This is the ONE item with real genetic routes, because fin proportion is the trait this project studied. But no route reaches the required magnitude: the largest measured increase in pectoral fin area from any single manipulation is +65% of wild type (hhip loss of function at 72 hours post fertilisation), and the requirement is +290%, a 3.9-fold area. Nothing in the fetched literature multiplies a fin's area by 3.9, and no manipulation was measured as a span or an aspect ratio at all, so the shape requirement has no sourced route even where the size one partly does. Combining levers is untested: the one double mutant that changes fin proportion (kcnh2a with lat4a) redistributes size between fins rather than scaling one fin up.

items.requirement: a large aerobic pectoral flight muscle at about 16% of body mass, where the real fish has small fin muscles
items.verdict: PARTIAL for 'more muscle', NONE for 'a pectoral muscle at 16% of body mass'. Myostatin loss of function is a real, repeated, quantified genetic route to extra skeletal muscle in teleosts: 16% more skeletal muscle in a CRISPR mstn-knockout red sea bream breed, 21% higher body weight in TALEN mstnb-/- zebrafish, 29.7% higher body weight with more muscle cells in CRISPR MSTN channel catfish, 41% more back muscle in male CRISPR MSTN olive flounder, and significant gains in medaka, common carp and antisense-knockdown Nile tilapia. Four reasons it does not reach the requirement. (i) Every one of these is an INCREMENT on existing muscle, not an allocation: the red sea bream '16%' is a 16% increase in total skeletal muscle, which is not the same quantity as a muscle equal to 16% of body mass, and no fetched source reports pectoral fin muscle as a fraction of body mass in any fish. (ii) Every one of these is axial/trunk muscle. No fetched source reports mstn loss, or any other manipulation, enlarging the pectoral fin musculature; the only fin-muscle genetics found (met, six1a/b, six4a/b, tbx5, lbx1) is loss-of-function reducing fin muscle, with no gain-of-function in the other direction. (iii) The mstn effect in fish is predominantly hyperplastic and the link from fibre number to mass is not reliable: transgenic dominant-negative MSTN medaka doubled muscle fibre number with gross muscle mass unaltered, and the authors state MSTN loss of function failed to induce double-muscling in medaka. (iv) The side effects are concentrated exactly where a flight muscle needs support: short body and small centrum in red sea bream, fewer and shorter vertebrae in yellow catfish mstnb knockouts, and fat accumulating inside the muscle in zebrafish and tilapia. For scale, the most aerobically specialised teleost measured here, juvenile Pacific bluefin tuna, carries only 3.77-10.69% of body mass as red muscle in total, over the whole body.

bat_comparison.source: PMC10966098 (Onychonycteris paper, 10.1038/s42003-024-06032-9) citing Bullen and McKenzie 2004: flight muscle on average 9.13 % of body mass in extant bats, minimum 7.8 %

what_is_missing: Every fin-muscle result this thread has is about whether muscle forms, not about its mass fraction: the pax7 quadruple mutant develops muscle-less pectoral fins, and met is necessary for the abductor.
A larger muscle is useless here unless it is aerobic rather than glycolytic, and fibre-type specification is a separate question from mass.

Mass-specific aerobic POWER is the quantity the physics needs, and no genetic result in this literature reports it: genetics reports fibre type, mitochondrial content or mass, never watts per kilogram.
Nothing connects a fin-muscle mass change to a flight-capable power output.

items.requirement: oxygen delivery about five times the bat range per kilogram, by haemoglobin capacity and cardiac output
items.verdict: NONE. Three findings, all negative for the requirement. (1) Capacity: every fetched genetic result on fish globins runs downward. Icefishes lost both haemoglobin gene clusters through transposable-element-mediated deletion; Asian noodlefishes lost myoglobin outright and let haemoglobin, haptoglobin and hemogen deteriorate; Antarctic notothenioids reduced haemoglobin multiplicity to a single adult isoform with lower oxygen affinity; the icefish candidate gene FAAP20 is associated with LOW haematocrit. The zebrafish globin loci and their LCR give a well-mapped cis-regulatory handle (two loci, two developmental switches, GATA1/NFE2 motifs, reporter-confirmed LCR), and the Root effect is a demonstrated pH-driven unloading mechanism in fish swimbladders, but no fetched source reports any manipulation that RAISES blood oxygen capacity in a fish. (2) Pump: genetic routes to a bigger fish heart do exist, which is the one real positive here. Knockdown of miR-458-3p and miR-144-5p drives cardiomyocyte proliferation and enlarged heart development through bmp2 in an Antarctic icefish, and Tg(myl7:ATF3) zebrafish develop cardiac hypertrophy with increased cardiac cell proliferation. But the icefish route is compensation for having no haemoglobin at all, the zebrafish route is pathological (fibrosis, disorganised sarcomeres, long-QT-like dysfunction), and neither reports a rise in cardiac output or oxygen delivery. (3) Magnitude: measured fish performance is not close. The highest fetched fish maximum oxygen uptake is 781.31 +/- 16.50 mg O2 kg-1 h-1 with a maximum cardiac output of 69.12 +/- 2.39 ml min-1 kg-1 in schoolmaster snapper, i.e. roughly 9 ml O2 kg-1 min-1 by this agent's arithmetic, reached by raising heart rate and tissue extraction rather than stroke volume, and the fish envelope plateaus at about 1.75-fold resting cardiac output and 2.5-fold extraction in salmon and tilapia on warming. No fish in any fetched source approaches the per-kilogram oxygen delivery the physics thread asks for. I deliberately fetched no mammalian baseline, so the exact multiple belongs to the physics thread; the point for this thread is that the shortfall is not marginal and that no genetic route in the fetched literature addresses it.

bat_metabolic_power_per_weight_W_per_N.source: PMC10154928: weight-specific metabolic power 7.1 to 18.7 W per N

what_is_missing: This thread's own data say nothing about oxygen delivery: the genotype map covers anatomy and gene links, not physiology.
No bird comparison is permitted here (Aves is the project's held-out clade), which removes the usual source of flight-oxygen genetics.

The requirement is on a PRODUCT of three physiological quantities, about 26.44x over teleost values. No genetic result in this literature reports any of the three as a quantity, let alone their product: genetics reports globin repertoires and heart sizes, not cardiac output in litres per minute or arterial oxygen content.

items.requirement: a respiratory surface that works in air, since gills do not ventilate in air
items.verdict: Real fishes breathe air by at least 9 distinct routes, so the ANATOMY is not hypothetical at all: this is the one requirement of the four that living fishes already meet, repeatedly and in several unrelated lineages. The GENETICS is a different matter. 8 of the 9 routes have some genetics attached, but only 2 rise above correlation to a functional result, so for most routes the molecular account of how the surface is built is not available. And the decisive fact for this project: NOTHING is known for Beloniformes, the order containing flying fishes, halfbeaks and needlefishes, and nothing at all for Exocoetidae. The homology of the gas bladder and the tetrapod lung is accepted and now supported at the level of cell types, but the molecular account of the switch between them is incomplete and partly negative, so even the best-studied starting point does not give a route.

physics_numbers.note: the climb requires the oxygen flux in item 3 while airborne

what_is_missing: A gas bladder used for respiration conflicts with its use for buoyancy, which is a design cost, not a gene.
Carbon dioxide excretion happens at the gills in water breathers, so an air-breathing fish still has to solve it.
